reviews.text: In its delicate, poignant account of its travellers’ broken lives, Nomadland has a tenderness that you simply don’t find in most mainstream Hollywood filmmaking.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: With Nomadland, Chloé Zhao completes a trilogy of sorts that offers an authentic and empathetic portrait of the dispossessed of the American West.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao and Frances McDormand combine to deliver a stirring commentary on the economy today, that bristles with bravery.
reviews.author: Gautam Sunder

reviews.text: Anchored by a towering performance by Frances McDormand, this is one of the best films of the year and an incredible time capsule of a defining moment in American history.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Cinema peaked when Frances McDormand went in that five-gallon bucket.
reviews.author: Brandon Stanwyck

reviews.text: Zhao was made to make this movie, and McDormand was made to play Fran. The combination of these two powerful women has culminated in a modern masterpiece.
reviews.author: Sarah Cortinaz

reviews.text: Ultimately, it’s not hard to connect with everything you see on screen because you can understand every character like they were someone you know.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: This is truly her movie and she carries it on her shoulders without a single false note.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: An emotionally rich, painfully relevant film about the waning days of the American Dream.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Zhao is a master at capturing people and their stories in such an authentic way that is usually water-downed in movies.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: One of the great pleasures of Nomadland is the consistently shrewd and perceptive manner in which Fern’s hidden depths and flinty pragmatics defy expectations
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Nomadland is a sobering tale of survival within the wake of the greatest economic downturn since the Great Depression.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: Nomadland offers a contemplative, enlightening, touching story about a nomad's life, starring real-life people that make this film much more special. Gorgeous cinematography and a lovely score tremendously elevate the movie.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Joshua James Richards’ masterful cinematography shines in this intimate film, which transcends the portrayal of the bleak nomad lifestyle and instead delves into a captivating character study.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Zhao’s stunning, masterful work in Nomadland looks to be rewarded as one of the most unique and inspired choices by the Academy in this category...
reviews.author: Brett Doze

reviews.text: Members of the supporting cast are real-life nomads playing fictionalized versions of themselves. See this extraordinary piece of filmmaking...
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: Zhao’s follow-up to the brilliant The Rider hits every single mark dead center. It is an odyssey of real-life people symbolized in one person, encapsulated in Frances McDormand’s best performance since Fargo.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: Nomadland revels in stark realism, and the real people that are used really add to the atmosphere and overall feel of the film. The story ultimately becomes less interesting as it moves along...
reviews.author: Carlos Ovalle

reviews.text: Between non-fiction and non-documentary, Nomadland plays with the narrative shortcomings to dazzle us instead through contemplation... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Remarkably mindful, stoic, and just so beautiful.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Nomadland is an earnest and empathetic epic on an intimate scale, powered by Chloé Zhao's delicate direction and Frances McDormand’s poignant lead performance.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: By elevating our circumstantial compulsion to the nobility of a purpose, Nomadland transforms from a film of our times to a timely film.
reviews.author: Ishita Sengupta

reviews.text: From a Nevada desert through the South Dakota Badlands to the Pacific coast, “Nomadland” is a work of visual poetry, but it’s the human element at its core that gives it such an emotional pull.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Nomadland challenges us and presses on the most dire questions of our times. It examines what is left behind in the wreckage of our broken world.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: The magic of that bigger canvas is that you become a different person for having watched Nomadland. Knowing these people and places changes your perspective.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: What is presented as a fulfilling alternative lifestyle embraced by people living on the fringes of society becomes a portrait of a broken person using the road to escape her past and shield herself from emotional ties.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The cinematography beautifully captures the desolate landscapes and the wide-open terrain of this country.
reviews.author: Nick Boyd

reviews.text: We are terrified by the idea that, as Fern, we might have an incredibly frail appearance of stability. What would we do if life doesn't turn out the way we wanted it to? Nomadland provided the freedom we wanted in 2020. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Beautiful cinematography in an alienating film doesn't have much value... [Nomadland] ends up idealizing an unideal situation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: Featuring one of McDormand's best performances - a role she occupies deeply - and emotionally dissecting the economic terrors of backwater America, 'Nomadland' is one of the best of the year.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: This warmth and genuine appreciation of people and the many routes they take make Nomadland one of the best movies in Nevada's supply of road pictures.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: It ultimately reverts to homilies, offering a flinty, exciting character a bland third-act volte-face.
reviews.author: David Katz

reviews.text: Nomadland the movie gets lost in its own drift, and, simply, drops off the map.
reviews.author: Robert Koehler

reviews.text: Somber but never dismal, personal and yet enormous.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Nomadland is a film with a sensibility, a power and a security in its resources and searches that make an impact. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Trekking across middle America with an optimistic glint in her eye, Frances McDormand's Fern could come straight from a Springsteen tune...
reviews.author: Greg Wetherall

reviews.text: A highly recommended road-movie where the melodrama is supported with steel nails, avoiding any kind of easy solution and proudly raising the gaze of those who lost everything. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: But with its clumsy dramatic embellishments ... and kitschy, faux-lyrical interludes ... [the film] is a reminder that ambivalence is not at all the same thing as complexity.
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: In McDormand's marvellous incarnation [Fern] is difficult to understand, tight, untalkative, but also helpful to others, and given to smiling occasionally in ways that contradict her dryness.
reviews.author: Michael Wood

reviews.text: It is one of the best films so far about the impact of the recession because of the human angle it takes.
reviews.author: Tom Crowley

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's Nomadland mimics life scrupulously...
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: For while, essentially, this is the bleak story of Fern... it is Richards's horizon-spanning photography that reminds us that what we're actually watching is a modern-day western.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: McDormand produced the film too - her performance really is extraordinary.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: People will keep coming back to this film for years to come because its messages and themes are timeless.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Zhao digs up something fierce, a little sad, spurred on by a lovely sense of longing and belonging that could be the perfect palate-cleanser after the year we've all just had. Frankly, the open road never looked better.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Wander with beautiful, mournful 'Nomadland.'
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Come on down for a gen-u-ine American dystopia at the crossroads of end-of-empire and late-stage capitalism. Chloé Zhao's outsider's eye is hugely sympathetic but unhindered by knee-jerk patriotism.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Touching, wryly amusing and, like its unusual heroine, bracingly unsentimental.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: What's most striking about Nomadland is the almost incidental manner in which it tells its stories - eschewing strident dramatic crises or narrative lurches for something altogether more ambient.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: ...a valentine to Amazon's CamperForce and the warehouses in which the 'Force works....
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Not since Robert Redford in All Is Lost has a star performer carried an entire film through wordless looks and glances.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: [McDormand's] vulnerable but commanding performance anchored the film's balance of professional and non-professional actors that gives the film its distinctive blend of documentary and elegy, grit and grace.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Frances McDormand delivers a career-best turn in this gently meditative drama about the failure of the American dream.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Having now seen it twice, I think it's a picture worthy of admiration, but not necessarily love.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Life on the road has never been so tenderly captured, politically alive and profoundly moving.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: There's nothing actorly or movie-star-like about her performance; she exists in the moment yet puts her dramatic skills to use to give us a full sense of who this woman is from what she carries with her and what she discards.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The timing of its arrival in homes is ideal. As we take bigger steps out in the world again, writer-director Chloé Zhao's film manages to be poignant, questioning, and ultimately life-affirming.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Zhao's sweeping ode to a forgotten America captures a universal poignancy that holds true in a waning, uncertain world.
reviews.author: Debbie Zhou

reviews.text: Personally, I am fine with the more sentimental moments of Nomadland. Social realism needs the space to contain multitudes and contradictions, just as life does.
reviews.author: Nathalie Olah

reviews.text: Even if Zhao can be a little bit obvious in her emotional intentions, this character study is an interesting critique of the american dream. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Ruiz

reviews.text: Nomadland manages to be uplifting and depressing all at the same time.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: McDormand masters an unshowy integrity that rarely grates against her less seasoned costars.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The real magic [of cinema] is watching a film like this and not knowing how they pulled it off.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: On a human level and a technical level, this is up there with one of the best of the past few years.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: '...a haunting, depressing film about man's inhumanity to our fellow man or woman, a Grapes of Wrath for the new, withering century before us...'
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: ... a peek behind a forbidden curtain ironically hidden in plain sight... a different tale of conquering the West: self-reliance as a way of life where the destination is making it another day.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: 108 minutes of poverty tourism.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: In the end, Nomadland is not a systematic takedown of the American Dream, and it's certainly not an expose of Amazon. But it is a subtle and profoundly sympathetic exploration of the kind of life we usually don't see.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Nobody ever gets angry, raises their voice or votes for Donald Trump. They don't even say swears. Zhao has made 'The Grapes of Wrath' without the wrath.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Caught somewhere between gazing longingly at the past and squaring up to the future, Nomadland feels like the only film that stands a chance of saying all the right things.
reviews.author: Paul M. Bradshaw

reviews.text: As Fern, [Frances McDormand] pecks at conversation like a bird, and moves like a lizard, holding still as if to conserve energy before darting off suddenly. Her bravest choice is to embody the character's passion without always rendering it palatable.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: In the hands of these creators, fantasies about the West hold the seeds of something genuinely democratic, a powerful struggle of people to build a life of plenty and freedom together...
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: A sincere and emotional drama, intensely atmospheric and empathetic, melancholic and intimate, an elegy for the marginalized that does not fall into self-pity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's gaze... is clearly humanistic and understanding. With Fern and those who eventually encounter her. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: A parade of cynicism disguised as humanity where Zhao turns labor exploitation and poverty into an adventure across the American roads. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Frances McDormand [delivers a] genuinely sympathetic, lived-in performance as Fern - easily her career-best performance since her 1984 debut in "Blood Simple".
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Nomadland powerfully dramatizes the very human need to find connections in the face of desolation.
reviews.author: Rory Doherty

reviews.text: A stunning character piece that doubles as an indictment of America's forgotten peoples, Nomadland cuts deep.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: A beautiful and affecting film: a small scale, spare movie with a deep well of compassion at its centre. By movie's end, we've been exposed to something rich and human.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Zhao and McDormand have created a beautiful character study about the flipside of the American Dream.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: This is beautifully shot and told story - one that is distinctly American for fortunate and unfortunate reasons.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Spectacular cinematography by Joshua James Richards and music by Ludovico Einaudi, enhances the earthy, raw sentiment of the story and landscapes it observes.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: A piercing portrayal of displacement and self-discovery.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Tastefully directed and starring a Frances McDormand who is from another goddamn planet. Chloé Zhao makes magic in a film that is, quite simply, thrills. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: Nomadland travels beyond the obvious in its examination of what it means to be at home with a heap of privations.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: Under Zhao's empathetic gaze, Nomadland blooms into a haunting testimony to the forgotten communities of the industrial Midwest.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: On the map of cinema, I never expected to find an intersection joining the corners of Varda, Malick, and Sayles. Zhao strikes me as an artist who finds her films by listening.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: The story of the fictional Fern downgrades the stories of the real-life nomads to secondary status. (In a doc) Zhao's authorial intent might not have been as intrusive. In this docu-fiction form, there's a distance between her vision and her subject.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Nomadland is 21st Century Oscar-bait in its most shameless form - almost as eye-rollingly obvious in its intentions as some of those awards-friendly period dramas that the Weinsteins used to produce a decade or two ago.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: A must about how to life as and outsider with images that present the people as an extraterrestrial. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: It might not reach the same heights as 'The Rider,' but it's unquestionably a film of our time and a directing showcase for Chloe Zhao. [Film Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Zhao clearly loves her characters - the majority of whom are played by real nomads - but that affection leads her to romanticise what feels like genuine economic suffering.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: It's all so minimal... but undeniably magical, and undoubtedly of the moment.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Frances McDormand is so compelling as the character that it's tempting to declare that this is the best performance of her career. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nando Salvá

reviews.text: The film takes on an increasingly urgent necessity - we must start thinking seriously about how we're going to live in ever more catastrophic conditions, in terms of the environment as well as the economy...
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Frances McDormand is great in this. What else is new?
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: It truly challenges us to take the road less travelled, literally and metaphorically, and sets us thinking about why others have chosen to do so.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: In Three Billboards, Mildred essentially breaks bad. Nomadland is an extended view of a woman doing everything she can to avoid breaking down in a country that already has.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: An exercise in extreme compassion.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Like Tina Fey with Mean Girls and Charlie Kaufman with Adaptation., Chloé Zhao has taken a non-fiction book and, through cinematic alchemy, transformed it into a fictional feature film.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: One of the melancholy pleasures of Chloé Zhao's masterful new film Nomadland is determining where the fact ends and the fiction begins.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: Strange, affecting and melancholy, Nomadland leaves one with a lingering feeling of sadness for a society that is fraying at the edges, scattering small fragments across the map of America.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: McDormand's performance is exactly what you would expect from the Oscar winner: honest, vulnerable, and, at times, uncomfortable to look at straight-on.
reviews.author: Sylvie Baggett

reviews.text: Nomadland has no plot or subplot, no character or narrative arc, no easily discernible thesis or moral. It just kind of "is." It's The Grapes of Wrath without the wrath. So, you know, grapes... But grapes are good, I guess?
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A great American road film...
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: Ii could not have been made anywhere but the United States. The vast expanses of the Western desert, the purple mountains' chilly majesty, provide a stark, flat, unwelcoming setting for the story about retirees and other Americans living in their vans.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is a character study and a cultural glimpse at another side of economic struggle and freedom.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Nomadland takes audiences on a raw, real, wondrous journey...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Strangely hypnotic in its simplicity.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: an astonishing piece a work-a film that is both simple and profound, a genuine heir to the principled spirit of Italian neorealism
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Zhao's craft here is unparalleled, and Joshua James Richards' cinematography utterly astonishing.
reviews.author: Amanda Jane Robinson

reviews.text: It's dreamy, even spiritual, to see characters left behind by mainstream society unspool their lives against the American West's abundant beauty.
reviews.author: Jas Keimig

reviews.text: Nomadland treats its subjects with respect and curiosity. Their misfortunes are not used to objectify or other them, as often happens in movies about an impoverished subculture.
reviews.author: Lidija Haas

reviews.text: Underneath a shell that alternates between wariness and basic decency, Fern's inner strength is never in doubt; whether that will be enough to survive in this world is the tension that drives this film
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: I don't use the word "masterpiece" very often, but Nomadland deserves the appellation here, for sure.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: Nomadland works on its own uniquely seductive level, which is closely tied to McDormand's extremely seductive performance.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Nomadland is one of the most understated and quietly painful films I have seen.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: The movie is beautifully made. It's also heartwarming bull ... This is the nicest movie about homelessness, financial despair and human frailty you'll ever see.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Nomadland is a rich and rewarding character-driven film that blends almost documentary-like observational scenes of Fern's encounters with the people that she meets on the road with moments of sublime beauty.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: Nomadland doesn't aestheticize poverty so much as it messily depicts the characters' connection to their nomadism.
reviews.author: Hazel Cills

reviews.text: McDormand ... gives a gripping, authentic, world-weary performance.
reviews.author: Josh Davis

reviews.text: In her third feature film, Chloé Zhao's Nomadland presents an America many of us don't want to see, but it's one that we should recognize with wide-open eyes.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: Nomadland is a film that revels in moments of quiet, yet its power is considerable.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: 'Nomadland's' willingness to shine a light on a shadowy alternative lifestyle and its use of non-actors make the film uniquely relevant and emotionally affecting.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Phenomenal. A director we'll hear about for a while to come...a great opportunity to catch her before she makes that big leap, I think people will really enjoy it.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: It's a staggering portrait of a community searching for grace after being ravaged by American capitalism, and Zhao's greatest work yet.
reviews.author: Cassidy Olsen

reviews.text: This story of a woman living out a life of quiet desperation is depressing and slow, teeming with shots of Frances McDormand thinking.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's Nomadland is a reminder that we can change at any age, meet new people along the way and know that whoever we're missing, we'll see down the road.
reviews.author: Brigid Presecky

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is a well-made movie with the feel of a documentary, but it depressed me out of my gourd. What else should I feel about the current state of elderly Americans forced into living Steinbeckian, migrant lives of survival with no hope in sight?
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: There's a genuine and emotional sense of presence as the viewer moves with Fern through the beautifully realized environs of Nomadland.
reviews.author: Alison Lanier

reviews.text: Fern hits the road in her mobile home initially to pick up work in a gargantuan Amazon warehouse, a symbol of 21st-century postmodernity as dehumanising as any 19th-century cotton mill or factory.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: Journalist and consulting producer Jessica Bruder's nonfiction book, "Nomadland: Surviving America in the Twenty-First Century," is livelier and more compelling than the film based on it.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: It's the faces and stories of [the] non-actors who make Nomadland soar.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Zhao's film, however accidental, is the empathy machine we need to get us through the pandemic. For that, it will live eternal.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: The pacing was excruciating...the performance left me underwhelmed and impossible bored
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: "Nomadland" feels simultaneously like both a memory and a prophecy. Zhao has managed to marry these juxtaposing ideas in her film, which is the essence of bittersweet distilled into an arrow and shot straight through the heart.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Zhao artfully showcases both the supportive community of vandwellers and the intense isolation of the lifestyle. Fern's loneliness is magnified against the stunning natural landscapes she visits.
reviews.author: Chelsea Steiner

reviews.text: [A]n intimate epic of the American west...quiet and expansive all at once, a film enamored of the broad openness of the landscape while gently acknowledging how easy it is for individual lives to get lost in the vastness that is America.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: If you're thinking about it after, it's probably worth watching, and all credit due to Zhao for this lyrical journey.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Frances McDormand makes us care in a role where her soul is bare. For me, 'Nomadland' is poetry in motion.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Frances McDormand is in an acting class of her own, able to communicate worry, resilience, loneliness, and the opposite -- with a subtle gesture, a shift of expression, a set gaze.
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: Though not much happens in this film, there's plenty to mull over and reflect upon. Chloe Zhao's film is a study of restraint in its minimalism, stripped bare of frills in terms of special effects or unnecessary dialog, but done to great effect.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is one of the best recent films to capture the very spirit of the times for those left behind by the economy.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: A beautiful audiovisual poem that captures the power of the human spirit and that explores the pain that keeps us moving forward. The best film of 2020. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Intimate and almost disarmingly tender and thoughtful, as every movie made by Zhao proves.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: The focus is on McDormand's Fern ... but Zhao's valentine to the disenfranchised is inclusive and communal in every way America is not.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: [Director Chloé] Zhao not only nails this American story, she revolutionizes it.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Director Chloé Zhao creates a beautiful palette for Nomad Fern to journey into, and her deliberate pacing mirrors that of a traveler with no destination. What is life anyway?
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The dark side of the American dream [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Frances McDormand is a first among equals in this mixture of the real life players and the actor cast.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: In the end, "Nomadland" delivers a liberal-libertarian longing for a vague, undefined restoration of what was.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is a chronicle of the Great Recession that plays like a quietly thoughtful, real-life "Grapes of Wrath," with McDormand's Fern as its understated Tom Joad - strong, resolute, haunting.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: The American social safety net looks like frayed wedges of tissue paper.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: It's slow-moving, but "Nomandland" is elegantly understated and effective.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: That is the challenge of this approach: committing to the [neorealist] aesthetic but relying on a star to carry it.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: It's just so deeply felt, moving, meditative, compassionate and beautiful. It's both majestic and kind of mundane.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: "Nomadland" balances with spine-tingling grace between respect for that restlessness of spirit and longing for a society that has any notion of how to care for it.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: They're enamored with the vast spaces that greet Fern as she joins fellow travelers on society's margins, and their kaleidoscopic overview makes for an engaging watch. They've crafted slice-of-life realism with the glossy sheen of a coffee table book.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Nomadland a lovely, poetical film that is not plot-driven, but so cannily crafted that it never feels meandering.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: What Zhao accomplishes is a beautiful blend of fictional storytelling and documentary filmmaking.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Nomadland is achingly beautiful and sad, a profound work of empathy from Zhao. It's a true elegy, a lament for the dead, a yearning for the lost.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: How Nomadland ends isn't really the point; it's about the journey and disconnected people connecting, finding solidarity in their transient way of existence.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: In the hands of a lesser filmmaker, life in an Amazon fulfillment center could've been raw material for mockery or, perhaps worse, pity.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: A remarkable film featuring a remarkable performance.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A road movie like no other, Nomadland is a modest masterpiece like no other. Beautifully unadorned and heart-in-your-mouth stirring, it's leisurely yet urgent, with a singular tone that lies somewhere between elegy and hope.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Zhao's movie is really defined by its texture and tone, and there's not a whole lot of meat or momentum to the story. Ultimately, it's a window into a way of life that will seem foreign to most in the modern age.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: A fiction film, it's inspired by a nonfiction book. But it also plays like an epic myth, set in spectacular landscapes John Ford movies made famous.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: The affecting, uneven Nomadland, set early in 2011 in the wake of the Great Recession but equally pertinent today, is a road movie of a very special sort.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Turn on (your engines) tune in (your radios) and drop out. Film mines appeal of alternate lifestyle.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Hit the road with Nomadland. It's a journey you won't forget any time soon.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: A Western without horses or violence ,Nomadland is one of those rare films that trusts the audience to see the poetry in an ordinary woman living an unorthodox but ordinary life. It trusts us to divine the courage in Fern.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: One of the best films of 2020. (Full Content Review for Parents - Full-frontal Nudity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The mix of McDormand and Strathairn with non-professional actors is often distracting, but the film's beauty and soulfulness nevertheless shines through.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Frances McDormand is more than capable of acting alongside non-actors, and her gifts become more necessary as we learn what drives the complex character she portrays.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Cuts to the heart of existence, resonating in tone and texture with the aches we all feel-even if the specific story it tells is far from our particular context.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: Fern - who has no children of her own - is suddenly handed a baby to tend to, and we see twitches of emotional confusion passing across her face, like the pastel clouds that drift across the big desert sky above.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Nomadland﻿ might tell an unconventional story, but thanks to Zhao's careful hand and McDormand's performance, it will resonate with all audiences.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: Nomadland takes a fascinating look at the modern-day nomads featuring gorgeous direction from Chloe Zhao and a powerhouse performance from Frances McDormand.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Fern and McDormand are... a window into a painful corner of America that is all too easy to look away from. Good for Zhao for pointing her camera directly at it.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: This is an elemental film in which everyday conversations and actions - and even gthe pauses the punctuate them - hold tremendous weight.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: The movie also contains scenic grandeur -- deserts, plains, forests -- and Zhao derives superb human-connection moments from her cast. These can be profoundly moving. McDormand helps bring about the magic.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: It feels human. It is human. And it's the best film of the year.
reviews.author: Mia Vicino

reviews.text: McDormand disappears into Fern, which is no small accomplishment for an actor as recognizable as she is.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: McDormand turns Fern into a great protagonist, but she lacks narrative direction. By the end, Nomadland frustratingly wanders off the edge of the map.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: There is great power in this movie's subtle choices, and what they add up to is an astonishing achievement in American film.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: In a fine Emersonian spirit, the movie rebels against its own conventional impulses, gravitating toward an idea of experience that is more complicated, more open-ended, more contradictory than what most American movies are willing to permit.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Frances McDormand poignantly haunts the American West.
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is the kind of big and big-hearted movie - featuring a central performance at once epic and fine-tuned - that reminds you of how much life one film can hold, when circumstances allow.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Like the nomads it spotlights, where the film thematically starts is not where it ends up.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: Zhao's screenplay ... doesn't strike a single insincere note, [and] I'm grateful for the opportunity to follow Fern and her friends on their journey.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Frances McDormand and Chlo Zhaoshow the aching beauty in life stripped down to the bone.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Writer/director Chloe Zhao centers on a world of transient folks who make it on their own in gorgeous Western landscapes. Headed by Frances McDormand, the cast includes a few real American nomads who seem like natural actors, too.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: An extraordinary film of stillness and contemplation that explores the journeys of a woman put onto the road by circumstance, which becomes her identity.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: To be sure, there is a nobility to "Nomadland," yet Zhao's film seems burdened by it.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Zhao's blend of reality and poetry is an aesthetic that will move some, while boring others, but...an empathetic portrait of itinerant Americans who, though confronted by tough economic times, refuse to give up or give in.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Like much of the land that Fern travels to and through, Nomadland is both desolate and beautiful. As the best movies do, it gives a glimpse into a world with which many people may be unfamiliar, and draws us in with a fascinating and emotional story.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Scripted and directed by Chloe Zhao, this adaptation of Jessica Bruder's nonfiction book feels like a true original, heartwarming without sentimentality.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: The contemplative "Nomadland" whispers instead of shouts its grievances about contemporary American life, and is all the more powerful for it.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: if there's a project out there that most appropriately captures the mood of 2020, it's Nomadland, a profound and elegiac meditation on loss - and on the process of moving on.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: With the breathtakingly stunning cinematography and magnificent score, I often found myself forgetting that this story is in fact heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: Zhao has emerged as a brilliant storyteller, able to convey a lot of emotion in such a subtle way you don't even realize the wallop till a while after it's hit you.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The invaluable David Strathairn deserves best supporting actor consideration for his beautifully understated performance as the road-weary nomad Dave...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is one of the very best films of 2020, one that works as both a compelling and eye-opening look at a segment of American society that is too often kept to the margins.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: The film vibrates with moral seriousness, but it misses all the best qualities of the book, where one learned about the ingenuity of the houseless as much as their plight.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Each stories of friendship and human connections are also extremely touching without being ever succumbing to cheap sentimentality. Too bad that music goes all extra gooey. With Zhao's documentary aesthetic of the film doesn't really need any soundtrack.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: [Chloe] Zhao, like Kelly Reichardt (whose Wendy and Lucy is spiritual kin to this film), has a knack for gazing on the deeds of marginalized people with the greatest delicacy and empathy, without turning preachy or polemical.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: As she salutes the resilience of humankind, Zhao has given us something genuinely unforgettable.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Zhao shows us the difficulty of this life - the endless laundromats, the cramped bed in the van, the cold, the possessions left behind - but also its beauty and freedom.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: A quiet and affecting study of people on the margins of society, with beautiful cinematography of the American west and a melancholy but hopeful tone.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: McDormand's performance might just be the best of her storied career.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao and Frances McDormand are a match made in film heaven.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: It is a serious mistake, a terrible irresponsibility ... to turn the social into the "natural" and inevitable ... One becomes an apologist for the existing state of affairs.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: This is the kind of film that gets widely lauded for its "empathy," but how far does empathy actually get us with these kind of social problems?
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: "Nomadland" is an existential exploration of the notion of freedom, of life lived on the blurry edges of American society, untethered to traditional ideals of society.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Don't look for anything like "Grapes of Wrath". This takes old people in RV's roaming the country in search of low-paying jobs and makes it seem as cool as "Easy Rider". A total fraud.
reviews.author: Louis Proyect

reviews.text: Zhao captures these landscapes (from the open road to the vastness of an Amazon packing center) with such a keen eye for the loneliness and freedom of this sort-of lifestyle
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: A sublime combination of reality and fiction, "Nomadland" is a perfect continuation of director Chloé Zhao's naturalistic story-telling approach.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A graceful elegy and a hopeful portrait, Nomadland -- like Zhao's The Rider before it -- is a new standard for the American western.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Zhao's patient and tender drama is as comparable as it gets to embarking on a long, meditative bike ride. It teaches us to embrace the world's natural state, with all its ups and downs.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: I was left speechless by the end of Chloe Zhao's Nomadland. It's fascinating, a film stripped down of everything.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Exceptionally small and simple - and uncommonly un-cinematic.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: No one is able to evince the beauty of America's heartland, and the decency, grit, and grace of its people, quite like Chloe Zhao...
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: Nomadland, with its nods to Terrence Malick, transcendental masters, and the overwhelming splendor of the natural world, feels like a movie out of time and right on time.
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: It has beautiful shots and moments that make me wonder about the human side of things as I observe the journey of that lonely nomad that is masterfully played by Frances McDormand. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Zhao's film is a a poetic Malickian ode to the pioneering nature of the restless American spirit.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Zhao places the failed promises of the American dream alongside some of its most beautiful, breathtaking vistas, as Fern pursues a life that isn't driven by a search for success and wealth.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: The rawness of every performance, non-fictional or otherwise, imbues the film with a sense of immediacy that gives rise to irrepressible anger.
reviews.author: Farah Cheded

reviews.text: McDormand gives one of the quietest, most powerful performances of her career as a woman living on and discovering the joys of the road in this affecting, memorable drama.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Through these characters, Zhao is able to examine the idea of wide-open frontiers without nostalgia or the need to pathologize the parts of our social structures that are eroding or have failed.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: It's great filmmaking from a talented director, and one of the industry's best performers.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Nomadland's clarity of thought on the concept of home, the environment, on women, on the elderly in society, on the very idea of human kindness, make this film much more than a passing moment.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: A beautiful depiction of an often-ignored group of people....With memorable performances and a visually gorgeous tour of America's West, Nomadland is a beautiful road trip down into a little-seen part of the country.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: A film I long to see in the post-pandemic world on a bigger screen where the film's universality can be lived into even though the story itself feels intimate and small.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: It's very much its own thing, very much an original experience, and must be counted as some odd kind of good movie.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: ... if there's aridness in the landscape, then barely none of it inhabits the heart of these compassionate travelers.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The best part is the gorgeous scenery we see as Fern travels the country. While I understand what this movie is trying to do, it is too slow and depressing for my liking.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Nomadland looks both sociological and touristy; it's a visual lecture teaching America to pity itself.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: As an evocative portrait of a largely forgotten people living on the margins of the American economy, this film is nearly flawless ... a stunning tour de force for Chloé Zhao and Frances McDormand.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A poetic and empathic journey about finding a sense of belonging and community. Frances McDormand's performance is extraordinary. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: In the face of Hollywood's drought of humane Cinema comes an understated exposé of staggering editorial substance.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Zao has a deep understanding of the unconventional, transient society that's seen a boom during recent hard times in our country, and she treats her restless characters with a poetic respect.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: It's quiet and spare in a way I admired more than I actively loved.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: A captivating, immersive and deeply emotionally intelligent character portrait
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: More than most road movies, this is a series of brief encounters, of short, intense friendships and sad farewells. As Wells says, "I'll see you down the road."
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The least actressy of actresses, McDormand merges completely with the landscape and everybody in it. The friendships that Fern makes spring from a collective store of commonsense gained from experience and coloured with playful good humour.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: A journey of discovery, a life lived on your own terms -- conventional or otherwise -- this story is both panoramic and intimate.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Zhao and McDormand have created a character and an existence for someone that I'd like to revisit periodically in the coming years.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Zhao's powerfully poetic drama cements her as a groundbreaking talent, shaking the earth with her work's hushed intensity.
reviews.author: Katie Duggan

reviews.text: Backed by a beautiful film score from Italian composer Ludovico Einaudi, Nomadland pulls you into this world and makes you feel part of it.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: An emotionally-charged masterpiece, Nomadland is a celebration in owning your happiness - in whatever form that may be.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: A neo-realist masterpiece.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: There shouldn't be any fudging around the fact that while Nomadland is a moving and absorbing portrait with a lot of heart, that heart is a singularly heavy one...So don't be surprised, or ashamed, should you get a bit misty-eyed.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's beautiful portrait of the human condition reminds us of the sweet lemonade that can be made from the bitterest of lemons.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Personally, I found it to be pretty much the perfect film for 2020; a paean to all people who have re-examined their lives, shifted their priorities and rediscovered the profound magic of empathy and quiet resilience. You'll quite probably love it too.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's thoughtful balance of majesty and intimacy makes Nomadland one of the most accomplished films of the year, an emotional tour de force that moves you but never imposes or manipulates.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The fictional principal character in Zhao's Nomadland, Fern (Frances McDormand), provides structure to a film composed largely of small incidents and stories shared by Americans who live on the road...
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's third feature is a love letter to nature's restorative energy and to the pioneers who brave their own trails.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: A uniquely American struggle is met by an indomitable American spirit in Nomadland...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Exploits pandemic free spirit escapist fantasy - somehow traveling the Trump train making US socio-economic misery great again. No need for statistics on homeless female murders and rapes, and with essentially characters hugging and kissing their poverty.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: The partial romanticisation of life on the road doesn't sit entirely comfortably with a more sobering character study and wider political commentary, never quite feeling the sum of its commendable parts as a result.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Frances McDormand's performance in "Nomadland" is the closest thing I've seen to Harry Dean Stanton in "Paris, Texas."
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Zhao presents it without flourish or hype. Like Fern, the film demands to be taken as it is.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Even if this is how Chloé Zhao misses the mark, "Nomadland" could never be mistaken for a film that's unworthy of time or attention. When this kind of skill and vision is so beautifully, compassionately blended, it deserves both.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: A hybrid between drama and fly-on-the-wall doc, this astonishing film takes a journey through an unseen segment of US society.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: McDormand is great. The movie wanders in the worst sense of the word.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: ...a mixed bag. It definitely has its moments and is at its best when dealing with mortality and loss rather than friendship...there's an implicit sentimentality about the film's overall style which can be tiresome.
reviews.author: Mark Demetrius

reviews.text: Nomadland is a movie about the picturesque places you'll probably never see and the struggling inhabitants of those places you might not ever think about.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Zhao once again relies on mixed methods, non-fiction rendered into compellingly realistic drama thanks to a cast of non-professional actors playing versions of themselves. The result is as stimulating and satisfying as it is iffy and curious.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: The beautiful cinematography, the charm of the supporting cast, and McDormand's faultless performance make it a gripping and deeply emotional watch from start to finish. It will leave you stripped bare and feeling raw in the best way possible.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Fern works at an Amazon plant to afford a life with no fixed address. The bitter irony that she prepares packages she could never herself receive is especially felt during the pandemic.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: This modern American road trip movie is the kind of expansive, meditative film that demands the same kind of physical space as a blockbuster, along with patience and compassion -- which is something we could all use more of these days.
reviews.author: Jenni Miller

reviews.text: Plays like a great American novel - one full of heart, compassion and empathy.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: 'Nomadland' is a physical and emotional journey as Fern ponders her choices. Though always moving forward, she also seems to be looking back at her old home and life.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The stunning cinematography and stunning performance from Frances McDormand aren't enough to push this over-the-line of great for me. Something is missing in the film's message.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Nomadland is a humanist masterpiece ... This is a quiet film, but never a dull one, with shots and themes that will continue to resonate ...
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: The anti-"Hillbilly Elegy", favoring reality over trite dramatics. Every frame of this movie pulses with meaning about contemporary America. One of the finest films of the year.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A Grapes of Wrath for the 2020s... not only evokes the visual language of John Ford and Terrence Malick, it stands beside those directors' very best work.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: A powerful testament to the times we live in, Nomadland is a beautiful, unforgettable film, worthy of any and all praise, and a masterclass in storytelling by the inimitable Chloé Zhao.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: At once loving and heartbreaking; an aching portrait of 21st century economic malaise that centers some of the truly forgotten men and women who live in the margins of the most prosperous nation on earth.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: 'Nomadland'is sort of a modern-day, existential equivalent ofWalden Pondset in the American West. The promise Chlo Zhao showed in'The Rider'three years ago is fulfilled here...with a little help from one of the finest actresses on the planet
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Nomadland is a great American film that represents people who haven't achieved the great American Dream in the traditional sense but are surviving on their own terms.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Zhao's gentle, open-eyed direction blends things as well as anyone could ask for.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The film is very slow moving and sparse, but incredibly engaging.
reviews.author: Paula Farmer

reviews.text: Zhao's direction is so matter-of-fact that we sometimes fail to realize the marvelous moments she has put before us, especially Joshua James Richards' cinematography and Ludovico Einaudi's piano-heavy musical score.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Frances McDormand inhabits Fern... It's an earnest, grounded, immersive performance in a quiet movie that portrays "flyover country" as a landscape where independent spirits can still strike out on their own.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: I tend to see [Zhao's] work as closer to later-period Terrence Malick, whose "Modern Life Is Rubbish" trilogy (To the Wonder, Knight of Cups, Song to Song) strikes a similar chord of melancholy restlessness.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: A patient and touching portrait of life lived on the fringes, of luxuriating in fleeting moments of connection in the face of enduring struggle, all from a woman about to waste her time making a Marvel movie.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Frances McDormand proves, once again, that she is the master of stoic characters whose study of life's challenges is subtle, but evident, on her face. This film is a treatise on the economy, aging, family, friendship, health care, and self identity.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Moody, introspective, and meditative, Nomadland makes up for its meandering, sometimes maddeningly slow pace with its insights about human nature and its incisive portrait of indomitability.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao, the Chinese-born director of this wondrous work of art (Oscar, please), joins with a never-better Frances McDormand and a cast of real-life nomads to capture what inspires the human urge to roam. It's a new American classic.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: McDormand exists here in a state of being ... and of being absolutely present.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: As Zhao and McDormand patiently reveal throughout "Nomadland," Fern may seem dwarfed by the vastness of the plains, but we come to see her heart is as big as the mountains on the horizon.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Nomadland is concurrently a celebration of the pioneering spirit and an elegy for a frontier that may have never existed.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Nomadland is a stark and hauntingly poetic portrayal of poverty in America. It addresses a hard truth with unvarnished sensibility.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A melancholic, understated slice-of-life with an Oscar-worthy performance by Frances McDormand that compensates for the film's lack of unflinching emotional depth.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: What results is a nuanced portrait of free spirits who reject a culture that has rejected them.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: Director Chloé Zhao is to be commended for her deft ability to show humanity unabashedly in her work, as well as for her knack of visual storytelling using the simplest means.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: 'Nomadland' sits with you and leaves you to contemplate the fall of an empire.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: Nomadland is a metaphysical and spiritual odyssey that results in a truly transcendent experience, and one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Diego Andaluz

reviews.text: Nomadland will be a spiritual experience for some, just another movie for others. There is such beautiful sadness to the breathtaking cinematography that follows Fern from Nevada to Oregon to South Dakota.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Nomadland is cinematic alchemy, and without a doubt this year's first truly essential film. Chloé Zhao is a miracle.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: A moving, majestically cinematic, poignantly thought-provoking, gorgeously contemplative portrait of outlier America.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: "Nomadland" isn't quite the emotional experience it's meant to be, but Zhao has outstanding command of the feature's textures and locations, creative a vivid understanding of Fern's journey of self.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It is an achingly moving work of transcendent cinematic art which is, paradoxically, humble and confident, fanciful and true, a film of realist authenticity and formalist wonders.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: Zhao blends fiction and nonfiction seamlessly, always with a hunger for naturalism and authenticity.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Frances McDormand already has two Oscars, and might need to find space on her shelf for a third.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's timely migrant drama paints a subtle portrait of a resilient woman determined to survive - despite devastating loss. Frances McDormand is magnificent!
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Nomadland is a meditation on the meaning and value of the concept of home: Does it reside in a building? A vehicle? A family? A sense of security and belonging?
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's astonishing film about American nomads is remarkable for what it is as well as for where it takes us. Zhao brings us vividly into the world of men and women who live on and, in some cases, for, the road.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: There is great beauty in the wide, open spaces Fern ranges around in...but there is also a melancholy quality to this lifestyle - Fern is always...watching someone leaving... settles into your bones like a great piece of American literature.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It's as simple as real stories from real people illuminated that need to be heard now more than ever. Chloé Zhao continues to be one of the most gentle and empathetic filmmakers working today
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: A film so immersed in the iconography of modern Americana that it feels both like an evocation and stern rebuke of the paintings of Norman Rockwell.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The film and its main character have the same range of stamina and lethargy. Unvarnished prestige too has its limits.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Somewhere, inside this lovely and desperate movie, there's the ghost of a Western.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: One of the most beautifully empathetic films about the working class struggle.
reviews.author: Shane Slater

reviews.text: It's a harshly critical assessment of our nation's deterioration. Yet, Zhao remains a filmmaker who still believes in an individual's indomitable spirit to not lose themselves entirely in such malaise.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Zhao has created such a powerfully intimate film, made with rare empathy and beauty, one that invites you to sit by the campfire and listen to the stories of these quiet heroes.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: Frances McDormand gives an Oscar-worthy performance as Fern. She explores the fine line between running toward freedom and running away from heartbreak.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: With Nomadland, Zhao wants us to marvel at simple things, like nature. You might question your material possessions and attachment to them. And even if this year isn't possible, you're gonna feel the need to explore the planet. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: The filmmaker takes up the images of the North American genre par excellence, the western, to tell a deeply resonant story, full of nostalgia and captivating hope. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Iván Morales

reviews.text: Everything from the cinematography to the performances to the editing was just so beautifully done.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: Nomadland flourishes under the direction of Zhao, and bolstered by a brilliant performance from McDormand. It's a wonderful achievement and a beautiful testament to the American spirit.
reviews.author: Daryl MacDonald

reviews.text: Nomadland packs such emotion and heart into a script which feels almost effortless on screen. Film fans, cinephiles and awards season followers should definitely add this little gem to your lists. This isn't the last you'll be hearing over awards season
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: On paper, films about homelessness sound angry or strident, but this film is more about the sadness and loneliness that accompanies alienation.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: A gorgeous film about a little-known subculture.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: [Zhao's] movie gives a voice to the marginalised. If you listen hard, it might just change your life.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: One of Frances McDormand's best, which is saying something. Director Zhao balances sadness and beauty in this story, with actors and non-actors, in which every frame feels true.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: In the natural ebb and flow of life, what [Nomadland] represents is an open road slice of Americana, driven to poetic, profound, and empathetic levels by a tour-de-force masterclass by Frances McDormand.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Another accomplished and moving piece of cinema from Chloé Zhao, and a searching exploration of the need to belong in modern society - or the need to not belong
reviews.author: James Mudge

reviews.text: Nomadland paints a heartfelt portrait of a lifestyle and a fascinating community, but it's not a recruitment brochure.
reviews.author: Ciara Wardlow

reviews.text: Nomadland, with its beautiful simplicity, and wonderful performances, manages to be an elegant, profoundly moving film which shows the real value of living, rather than just surviving.
reviews.author: Zoe Margolis

reviews.text: Nomadland is a soulful character study from Chloe Zhao that features an awards-worthy performance from Frances McDormand as an untethered yet haunted traveller.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: Populated with real individuals (not actors) and an Oscar worthy take from the queen of cinema: Frances McDormand, filmmaker Chloé Zhao has concocted a small slice of film heaven, complete with small intricacies about finding yourself in unexpected ways.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The film takes place in the aftermath of the 2008 recession. But it might as well be in an alternate universe where no one speaks above a whisper and "America" remains a vaguely benign abstraction.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: Hopeful and human yet bathed in unmistakable melancholy, Nomadland isn't a film striving to be particularly profound, which is in many ways precisely why it is.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Driven by McDormand's complex performance, Nomadland is a breathtaking journey.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: An absolutely magical piece of work.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao and Frances McDormand combine for a heartfelt adventure through the American West in a tale brimming with life and empathy.
reviews.author: Redmond Bacon

reviews.text: The one noticeable departure for the director is her centering the film on a star ... McDormand adds Fern to her sisterhood of impish, cranky, fiercely stubborn, and opinionated women.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Nomadland inspires as much as it enriches. A loving ode to the pioneer spirit and the authentic experience of freedom
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: This is how the other half lives. The half that is most often neglected and growing in numbers.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's Nomadland is truly a work of art, a beautiful movie that restores your faith in film and life
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's films aim to form an intimate connection between people and land and Nomadland deals with this in both a literal natural sense in the character of Swankie and a metaphorical sense in Fern.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: Nomadland is perhaps one of the deftest works of cinema in recent years, transcendent simply by looking, unflinchingly, into the heart of the American character. It lets the characters, the landscape, and the images take the viewer where they need to go.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: McDormand holds Fern's grief, hope, and reflection in her eyes, and with every look or facial expression she allows us to get to know Fern a little more.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Over the course of the film, we are able to ascertain a sense of Fern's circumstances, but more specificity around her and other characters' daily struggles and successes would render Nomadland's narrative much more real and engaging.
reviews.author: Esmé Hogeveen

reviews.text: McDormand is incredible here and deserves the attention she's been getting. This film does shine a light on an important issue - I just wish it hadn't put quite such a positive spin on it.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: Nomadland is no stump-speech anecdote or soapbox sermon. It's too empathetic for that, too invested in the humanity of Fern and all those around her.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: For a film that aims to portray the plight of growing old in a country that offers little respite for aging populations... Nomadland is less interested in confronting this issue as it is painting a beautiful picture of an unlikely way of life.
reviews.author: Natalia Keogan

reviews.text: A timely tribute to forgotten Americans surviving the country's structural failures -- this film from a Chinese female director is more than worthy of making Oscar history.
reviews.author: Weiting Liu

reviews.text: The remarkable odyssey of a feisty woman who finds community and her true self in her home on the road.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Often bleak, occasionally heartwarming, and always poignant, Nomadland speaks not only to our time, but to the lost promise of the past.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Nomadland is a deeply internal and even mournful film in this regard, and asks its viewers to pause and reflect, like the listeners of a eulogy.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: Zhao has created a true work of cinematic art for our time, a sublime journey of the spirit and the soul of a woman and her country.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Zhao's style is evocative but accepting. 'Nomadland' is an exquisite gem of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: Nomadland is a wonderful exploratory mission into real American life. I can't wait for everyone else to see it.
reviews.author: Lorry Kikta

reviews.text: I enjoyed spending time with these characters (or character) but just enough to recommend it. I did not love it
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao makes Nomadland's melancholic but hopeful story of nomads traversing the American West a stunningly complex character study of life on the margins of society.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: A human experience that depicts how home is where the heart is, presented in the most cinematic way possible.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: [McDormand's] is a fascinatingly complex, almost entirely internal performance, and it's one of the year's absolute best.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: An emotive, lyrical picture about a woman who finds stability in impermanence, "Nomadland" cements Chloe Zhao's as one of the defining young voices in modern cinema
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: The film is a successor to John Ford's The Grapes of Wrath for the age of singletons, and like Ford's masterpiece, it sprinkles sentimentalization into grit so deftly that it's a marvel.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: McDormand delivers a clear-eyed quiet performance infused with her trademark no-nonsense demeanor and flashes of humor as she highlights Fern's stubbornness.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: ...this astounding work not only cements Zhao as a director to stay excited about, it positions her as a visual poet approaching the skill and lyricism of Terrence Malick.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: With The Rider and now Nomadland, it's safe to say that Zhao is the standard-bearer for the New American Western.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: [T]he combination of Chloé Zhao and Frances McDormand deliver a 1-2 punch.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: A revealing exploration of a harsh reality, humanized by sensible direction and mesmerizing acting. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Nomadland presents older characters, many living with disabilities, unvarnished but with endless empathy.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Nomadland could easily have been adapted from a Bruce Springsteen song, so true is it to the plight of the working man and woman.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The mostly non-professional actors are not intimidated by Frances McDormand's empathetic performance but turn out some splendid portrayals of their own.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: A hopeful portrait that raises existential questions, always granting the space and time necessary for everyone to find their own answers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Cristina Aparicio

reviews.text: The reason to watch "Nomadland" is to see first-hand Frances McDormand's heartfelt performance, one of the best of her career, and to bring the topic of nomad workers to the forefront. Look for Oscar buzz and many awards in the coming season.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Transcendental. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mariona Borrull

reviews.text: It really is a film you don't just watch -- you get on the same wavelength with it.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: At its heart, Nomadland is a road movie, but too many scenes feel stuck in neutral...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: [Chloé Zhao] expertly blends her professional actors with amateurs, essentially playing themselves. She has an expert touch in culling poignant performances from non-actors, which adds all the more verisimilitude to the film's mise en scene.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Nomadland is a radiant celebration of humanity and community.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: A role and story drawn from life, "Nomadland" feels like classic fiction.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Nomadland is indescribably enveloping.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Frances McDormand stars alongside a cast of real-life nomads.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: McDormand's commanding, deeply empathetic performance holds the film together.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: The two-time Oscar-winning best-actress... is at the top of her game in filmmaker Chloe Zhao's Nomadland.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: It's a profoundly moving, often unbearably beautiful piece of cinema that will nourish your mind and break your heart.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Zhao masterfully weaves a heart-crushing portrait.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: The philosophy of the travellers provides much food for thought, but Nomadland is also a movie you can truly watch, in the best sense of the word.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Frances McDormand offers us a masterful performance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Deceptively complex, lyrical, and very necessary, Nomadland expresses the quiet strength of its characters, and the life they have chosen, or was forced on them.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: It still feels unique because it captures a far bigger world without ever losing the intimacy between characters.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: McDormand is amazing as usual, but in a way that doesn't call attention to herself. She's not going for big dramatic "Oscar moments" but instead blends in perfectly with the actual nomads revealing their life stories.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao's 'Nomadland' is a portrait of a subculture who have chosen to escape from the unrealistic expectations of the capitalistic delusion.
reviews.author: Shea Vassar

reviews.text: ...embodied with heart and strength by Frances McDormand. Zhao's film scatters the shattered remains of the American Dream amongst the breathtaking vistas of the 'land of the free'; a romantic sonnet dedicated to a broken place.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Nomadland mines a poetic portrait from its well-textured subjects, showcasing writer/director Chole Zhao as a boundless talent with a bright future in the industry.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao continues to paint moving, melancholy portraits of the modern American West and the people who inhabit it.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: This movie is worth seeing specifically for Frances McDormand's performance, the beautiful cinematography, and also for the real-life nomads that the film includes.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: The journey Zhao has crafted is marvelous, exploring literal peaks and valleys as well as emotional ones.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: Nomadland is a near seamless pairing of filmmaker and actor, the two working in delicate harmony as they trace Fern's loose, bittersweet trajectory.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Nomadland is both a move in a bolder direction and an affirmation that [director Chloé Zhao's] been on the right road all along.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: Its gentle survey of humanity reminds me of another unlikely Disney movie, David Lynch's The Straight Story, which is no small compliment.
reviews.author: Bill Chambers

reviews.text: Zhao finds the beauty in it, the pain in it and all that lies between, making for a film full of remembrance, of joy and loss and, most importantly, of the significance of keeping on moving if your story isn't settled at your first destination point.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Here's a beaut.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It's an observant, simple, contemplative work, one uninterested in manufacturing melodrama or hyped-up incident, but rewarding for its illumination of Americans who represent societal afterthoughts.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: It's a melancholic journey of self-acceptance, resilience and prizes the clearheaded realities of solitude bolstered by an empathetic turn from McDormand.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Nomadland at times has the feel of a documentary, but with none of the earnest flatness that mars even some very well-meaning documentaries...
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Images of these displaced Americans persevering in the margins can at times make Nomadland feel like a modern day Grapes of Wrath, save McDormand's version of Ma Joad travels only with her ghosts.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Frances McDormand is Sublime in Chloé Zhao's Achingly Beautiful Drama.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's Nomadland is one of the best films you'll see this year: simple, elegant and beautiful, and built around a truly remarkable performance from Frances McDormand.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: [A] lean, sad, richly textured portrait of life on the American outskirts.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A quiet, slow, but profound film. Telling the story of one 60-something woman who is alone in life living a kind of life many would see as undesirable.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's Nomadland beautifully examines the transition from the circumstantial to the autonomous and paints a picture of humanity like we've rarely seen it on screen.
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: Elegiac journey through a broken America, anchored by yet another subtle and specific performance by Frances McDormand. Gently political, effortlessly poetic, its ambling, rambling nature will please many.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: Nomadland is a gorgeous, lyrical film featuring another stand-out lead performance by Frances McDormand. Chloé Zhao's latest is a testament to the beauty of the American Midwest and the value of living an unorthodox life.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: McDormand, who is in every scene, makes Fern as tough at the plant she named for in that she adapts and survives. The actress gives a committed performance that will likely garner her an Oscar nomination.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer
