reviews.text: ...a truly special, singular endeavor from an almost breathtakingly talented new filmmaker.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: [Nomadland] may flicker though Fern's transient existence with episodic regularity, but the kernels of its beauty lie in the collective expanses of that journey, which build and build with quiet intensity.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: In writer-director-editor-producer Chloe Zhao's searing new film, Frances McDormand plays Fern with a quiet ferocity, ultimately delivering a gut-punch of a performance.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Great acting is often about reacting and the reaction shots of Frances McDormand are the secret ingredient to Nomadland.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: By juxtaposing beautiful vistas filled with promise, a rotted social safety net, and the scrappy itinerant workers navigating the space in between, Zhao generates a gradually swelling tension underneath her film's somewhat placid surface.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao is back with a masterful work that will lead the awards conversation going forward. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: McDormand is still finding the little-told stories that lead to impactful cinema.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Nomadland plays as a cerebral character study, although not too focused on the state of mind to shy away from the beautiful scenery existing all around Fern.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A gorgeous film that's alternately dreamlike in the way it captures the beauty of this country and grounded in its story about the kind of person we don't usually see in movies.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: It's hard to imagine another American film this year that will be able to top NOMADLAND. A masterpiece.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Nomadland boasts one of the best leading performances of recent memory in a movie that will be hard to top for the title of best film of the year.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's incredible film finds beauty and humanity in the ruins of the Great Recession.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: A family is formed by way of a philosophy. New friendships are therefore a delicate process of boundaries and understanding. Zhao doesn't compromise that truth.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A beautifully told tale of courage and compassion, with Frances McDormand giving a career-best performance. This is essential, and one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Baby, Frances McDomand is letting us have it in the sucker punch gut wrenching drama based on the Jessica Bruder novel Nomadland. With exquisite, nuanced direction from Chloe Zhao
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: [Nomadland] is also a further refinement of Zhao's techniques, of the rough-hewn yet strikingly seamless weave of fiction and nonfiction...
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: An Elegy for American Exceptionalism: The nation built by frontiersmen always looked down on them. Rich White America lied to Poor White America all the while sneering at them. We of Brown and Black America never assumed differently.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: The melancholy lyricism of Nomadland is something truly special, and this quiet marvel of a film deserves your attention.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Nomadland is every bit as powerful [as The Rider]: an ode to pioneer spirit and a lament for the communities and lives that were decimated after the financial recession of 2008.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Nomadland cements Chloé Zhao as one of the finest directors today.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: A powerful character study of a different kind of freedom fighter.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: For the making of the film - which she wrote as well as directed - Zhao immersed herself in this subculture and she immerses us too.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: The sheer compassion of Zhao's direction is one of the film's most elemental pleasures, while McDormand is one of those rare actors who can somehow make the act of listening as thrilling as a barnstorming speech.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: [Zhao] is fast becoming one of our premiere chroniclers of a certain kind of forgotten American: raw-boned, untethered, on the margins.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The movie churns through a familiar saga of a woman who grows tired of her surroundings, but casts aside the pressure to conform to the traditional beats of that plight.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: There is real greatness in Chloé Zhao's film-making.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Watching "Nomadland" feels like gazing out on one long, gorgeous sunset. If that's not your thing, so be it, but for those on Zhao's wavelength, the movie is a marvel of empathy and introspection.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Even if your time is running out, that view never will, it will continually unfold out from itself, multiplying the acreage within: "Nomadland" is a gorgeous, endless unfurling.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

synopsis: Nevada kırsalındaki bir şirket kasabasının ekonomik çöküşünün ardından Fern, minibüsünü doldurur ve yola koyularak modern bir göçebe olarak geleneksel toplumun dışında bir hayatı keşfetmeye başlar.
